models.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (B)
models.credit: NASA/Brian E. Kumanchik; NASA/Christian A. Lopez
models.logoCheck: All five textures of the hand-built file looked at by the Data session on 2026-11-15: solar cells, wiring, foil, instrument close-ups and two colour ramps, no logo or insignia. The owner's own visual check is separate.
models.note: NASA's page for this model describes IBEX and names IBEX as its mission, although the model is titled Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. Which spacecraft it shows is being checked.

models.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (A)
models.statusNote: NASA's mission page gives its launch as June 18, 2009 and says it has studied the Moon from up close since 2009.
models.logoCheck: The built file has no picture textures, only one 128 x 4 colour palette, looked at by the Data session on 2026-11-15.

models.name: Lunar Atmosphere and Dust Environment Explorer (LADEE)
models.statusNote: NASA's mission page says it launched on Sept. 6, 2013 and that the mission ended on April 18, 2014, when it impacted the Moon as planned.
models.logoCheck: The built file has no picture textures, only one 128 x 4 colour palette, looked at by the Data session on 2026-11-15.

models.name: Lunar Laser Communications Demonstration (LLCD)
models.statusNote: NASA's page says the technology was demonstrated with LLCD from October 2013 through April 2014, during the LADEE mission.
models.logoCheck: The built file has no picture textures, only two 128 x 4 palettes (colour, metal and roughness), looked at by the Data session on 2026-11-15.

models.name: Habitat Demonstration Unit (part 2)
models.logoCheck: The one texture of the hand-built file looked at by the Data session on 2026-11-15, with a zoomed look at its small labels: panels, grilles and fittings, no logo or insignia. The owner's own visual check is separate.
models.note: NASA's page describes a Deep Space Habitat unit from NASA's Habitation Systems Project for future missions. It does not say whether it was built or tested.

models.name: Regolith Advanced Surface Systems Operations Robot (RASSOR)
models.credit: NASA/Dewey L. Smith; NASA/Jason M. Schuler
models.logoCheck: The file has no textures at all (one plain material), checked by the Data session on 2026-11-15.
models.note: NASA's page describes a robotic excavator for precursor landing missions. Neither it nor NASA's technology page for RASSOR (KSC-TOPS-7) says what was built or flown. It has not been to the Moon.
